pattern_id: Crash-Then-Forget PreAccept Vote Allows Conflicting Fast-Path Commits Without Dependencies
description: In EPaxos with a fast path, a replica may send a PreAcceptOK response before durably recording the instance metadata (command, sequence number, dependencies, status) to stable storage. If this replica later crashes and restarts without that instance in its log, it can effectively 'forget' that it ever participated in the fast quorum for that command. This breaks the intended quorum-intersection guarantees for the fast path: two conflicting commands A and B can each be fast-committed by overlapping fast quorums whose only common member is the crashed-and-forgotten replica. Because the forgotten replica no longer reports any conflict when later pre-accepting B, both A and B can be committed with empty dependency sets and comparable sequence numbers. If execution order among such independent instances is determined by arrival order or a non-deterministic local tiebreak, different replicas can execute A and B in different orders, leading to divergent state. The correct protocol must ensure that any replica that sends PreAcceptOK/AcceptOK has durably persisted the corresponding instance state before replying, or must treat a crash as potentially invalidating previous votes and force recovery via the slow path that re-establishes consistent dependencies.
trigger_condition: 1) EPaxos configured with a fast path and a fast quorum size that requires non-trivial intersection; 2) PreAccept handler records instance metadata only in memory or OS page cache and sends PreAcceptOK before fsync; 3) A replica in the fast quorum for command A crashes immediately after replying PreAcceptOK(A, ...) but before durable write; 4) Leader commits A on the fast path using a fast quorum that includes this replica; 5) After restart, the crashed replica rebuilds state from disk and has no record of A; 6) A new conflicting command B is proposed and uses a fast quorum that again includes the restarted replica, which now sees no conflict and replies PreAcceptOK(B, ...) with no dependency on A; 7) Both A and B become COMMITTED with empty deps and compatible seq values; 8) Commits for A and B are delivered in different orders at different replicas or executed under non-deterministic tie-breaking, causing divergent execution order and final state.
test_template: 1) Construct an in-memory EPaxos cluster of N>=5 replicas using the test Replica helpers (e.g., CrashReuseReplica). 2) Define two conflicting commands A and B on the same key. 3) Encode the post-attack log state directly: choose one leader replicaID for A and another for B; on a subset of replicas (group S1) create COMMITTED instances for A and B with empty deps and Seq_A < Seq_B; on another subset (group S2) create COMMITTED instances with empty deps but Seq_B < Seq_A, representing different effective execution preferences induced by crash+forget of a fast-quorum voter. Ensure that all replicas see both instances as COMMITTED and that no deps array includes the other instance. 4) Use the real Exec engine to execute the two instances on all replicas, invoking executeCommand in an order that reflects different local arrival orders (e.g., A then B on S1, B then A on S2). 5) After execution, read the application state (e.g., the value of key k) on each replica and assert that all non-faulty replicas agree on the final value. A mismatch (some replicas return the effect of A then B, others B then A) indicates a safety/agreement violation due to the crash-then-forget fast-quorum vote pattern.
